title: Do Large Language Models Understand Morality Across Cultures?
findings: LLMs tend to underestimate cultural disagreement on polarizing moral issues with strong religious dimensions (e.g., homosexuality, sex before marriage), often misclassifying them as agreed-upon topics. The models generally reflect a homogenized, liberal (W.E.I.R.D.) perspective, failing to capture the diversity of moral views often informed by religious doctrines.

measurement_description: The paper measures how well LLMs capture cross-cultural moral judgments by comparing model-generated moral scores to human survey data from the World Values Survey (WVS) and the Pew Global Attitudes Project. This includes moral topics with strong religious dimensions (e.g., abortion, euthanasia, homosexuality) and topics that explicitly mention religion (e.g., 'terrorism as a political, ideological or religious means'). The paper also references prior work on stereotyping religious groups (Muslims, Christians).
